cemc-gauss8-2004-01.title: Halve twice
cemc-gauss8-2004-01.body:
Half of 2004 is 1002 and half of that is 501.

**Answer: (B) 501**

cemc-gauss8-2004-05.title: Isosceles triangle
cemc-gauss8-2004-05.body:
The two long lines and the short slanted line form a triangle. The $30^\circ$ angle and the angle of the triangle at the crossing point of the two long lines are vertically opposite, so that angle is $30^\circ$. The tick marks show the two sides from that vertex are equal, so the triangle is isosceles and its other two angles are each $\frac{180^\circ - 30^\circ}{2} = 75^\circ$. The angle $x^\circ$ is on a straight line with one of these $75^\circ$ angles, so $x = 180 - 75 = 105$.

**Answer: (D) 105**

cemc-gauss8-2004-05.title: Exterior angle
cemc-gauss8-2004-05.body:
As above, the triangle has angles $30^\circ$, $75^\circ$, $75^\circ$. The angle $x^\circ$ is an exterior angle of the triangle, so it equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: $x = 30 + 75 = 105$.

**Answer: (D) 105**

cemc-gauss8-2004-06.title: Side lengths
cemc-gauss8-2004-06.body:
Each small triangle has side $6 \div 3 = 2$ cm. Each side of $\triangle ABC$ is made of 3 small sides, so it is 6 cm long and the perimeter is $3 \times 6 = 18$ cm.

**Answer: (A) 18**

cemc-gauss8-2004-06.title: Scale
cemc-gauss8-2004-06.body:
$\triangle ABC$ is three times as wide as a small triangle, so its perimeter is $3 \times 6 = 18$ cm.

**Answer: (A) 18**

cemc-gauss8-2004-08.title: List outcomes
cemc-gauss8-2004-08.body:
The four equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT. Only HH works, so the probability is $\frac14$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac{1}{4}$**

cemc-gauss8-2004-08.title: Multiply
cemc-gauss8-2004-08.body:
Each coin lands heads with probability $\frac12$, independently, so both do with probability $\frac12 \times \frac12 = \frac14$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac{1}{4}$**

cemc-gauss8-2004-09.title: Add the two parts
cemc-gauss8-2004-09.body:
From the surface down to sea level is 180 m, and from sea level down to the floor is 220 m more, so the depth is $180 + 220 = 400$ m.

**Answer: (D) 400 m**

cemc-gauss8-2004-09.title: Integers
cemc-gauss8-2004-09.body:
The elevations are $+180$ and $-220$, and the difference is $180 - (-220) = 400$ m.

**Answer: (D) 400 m**

cemc-gauss8-2004-11.title: Minutes per km
cemc-gauss8-2004-11.body:
At 5 km per 60 minutes she takes 12 minutes per km, so 1.5 km takes $1.5 \times 12 = 18$ minutes.

**Answer: (C) 18**

cemc-gauss8-2004-13.title: Number the trees
cemc-gauss8-2004-13.body:
Number the trees 1 to 13 from her house. On the way to school she marks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. On the way home she starts at 13 and marks 13, 10, 7, 4, 1. The unmarked trees are 2, 6, 8, 12: four trees.

**Answer: (B) 4**

cemc-gauss8-2004-13.title: Count the even trees
cemc-gauss8-2004-13.body:
After the morning, only the even trees 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 are unmarked. In the afternoon she marks trees $13, 10, 7, 4, 1$; of these only 10 and 4 are even. So $6 - 2 = 4$ trees stay unmarked.

**Answer: (B) 4**

cemc-gauss8-2004-15.title: Box minus the notch
cemc-gauss8-2004-15.body:
The solid is a $4 \times 5 \times 6$ box with a $1 \times 2 \times 4$ box cut out along the top edge (shown by the dotted lines). The volume is $4 \times 5 \times 6 - 1 \times 2 \times 4 = 120 - 8 = 112$.

**Answer: (B) 112**

cemc-gauss8-2004-15.title: Split into two boxes
cemc-gauss8-2004-15.body:
Cut horizontally at the bottom of the notch: the lower part is $4 \times 4 \times 6 = 96$, and the top layer of height 1 is missing a width of 2 out of 6, so it is $4 \times 1 \times 4 = 16$. Total $96 + 16 = 112$.

**Answer: (B) 112**

cemc-gauss8-2004-18.title: Use each condition
cemc-gauss8-2004-18.body:
The range is $10 - 6 = 4$; since 6 and 10 each appear once, removing either would change the range. The mode is 8; removing an 8 would leave 7 and 8 tied, changing the mode. So we remove a 7 or the 9. To raise the mean we must remove a score below the mean, so we remove the 7.

**Answer: (B) 7**

cemc-gauss8-2004-18.title: Compute the means
cemc-gauss8-2004-18.body:
The total is 63, so the mean is $63/8 = 7.875$. Removing a 7 leaves $56/7 = 8$ (higher); removing the 9 leaves $54/7 \approx 7.71$ (lower). So remove the 7.

**Answer: (B) 7**

cemc-gauss8-2004-19.title: Compare words
cemc-gauss8-2004-19.body:
CAT and CAR differ only in the last letter, and $12 - 8 = 4$, so R is worth 4 more than T. BAR differs from BAT in the same way, so BAR $= 6 + 4 = 10$.

**Answer: (A) 10**

cemc-gauss8-2004-20.title: Compare without decimals
cemc-gauss8-2004-20.body:
$AC = 5 = CD$, so (B) and (C) are both $5 + \sqrt{20}$, smaller than (E) $5 + \sqrt{29}$. $FD = \sqrt{85} < \sqrt{100} = 10$. For (A), $AE = \sqrt{106}$, while $(5 + \sqrt{29})^2 = 54 + 10\sqrt{29} > 54 + 10 \times 5 = 104$ and in fact, since $\sqrt{29} > 5.2$, it is more than $54 + 52 = 106$. So $AC + CE > AE$ and $AC + CE$ is the largest.

**Answer: (E) $AC+CE$**

cemc-gauss8-2004-21.title: One centimetre on the map
cemc-gauss8-2004-21.body:
1 cm on the map is $1050 \div 21 = 50$ km $= 5\,000\,000$ cm in reality, so the scale is $1 : 5\,000\,000$.

**Answer: (E) 1:5 000 000**

cemc-gauss8-2004-22.title: Amount poured
cemc-gauss8-2004-22.body:
The bottle went from full to $\frac34$ full, so $\frac14 \times 1.5 = 0.375$ L was poured. This fills $\frac34$ of the glass, so the glass holds $0.375 \div \frac34 = 0.5$ L.

**Answer: (A) 0.5 L**

cemc-gauss8-2004-22.title: Compare sizes
cemc-gauss8-2004-22.body:
$\frac14$ of the bottle equals $\frac34$ of the glass, so the bottle is 3 times as big as the glass. The glass holds $1.5 \div 3 = 0.5$ L.

**Answer: (A) 0.5 L**

cemc-gauss8-2004-23.title: Show the big triangle is isosceles
cemc-gauss8-2004-23.body:
The tick marks show $AD = BE$ and $AE = CD$. So $AC = AD + DC = BE + EA = AB$, and $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles with $\angle ACB = \angle ABC = 80^\circ$. Then $\angle BAC = 180^\circ - 80^\circ - 80^\circ = 20^\circ$. In $\triangle ADE$, $\angle AED = 180^\circ - 30^\circ - 20^\circ = 130^\circ$, and $x^\circ$ is supplementary to it: $x = 180 - 130 = 50$.

**Answer: (C) 50**

cemc-gauss8-2004-23.title: Exterior angle
cemc-gauss8-2004-23.body:
Once we know $\angle A = 20^\circ$ (as above), $x^\circ$ is the exterior angle of $\triangle ADE$ at $E$, so it equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: $x = 30 + 20 = 50$.

**Answer: (C) 50**

cemc-gauss8-2004-24.title: Place value
cemc-gauss8-2004-24.body:
$x - y = (100A + 10B + C) - (100C + 10B + A) = 99(A - C)$. So $99(A - C) = 495$ and $A - C = 5$. With $C \ne 0$: $(A, C) = (6,1), (7,2), (8,3), (9,4)$. $B$ can be any of 10 digits. That gives $4 \times 10 = 40$ possibilities.

**Answer: (B) 40**

cemc-gauss8-2004-24.title: Column subtraction
cemc-gauss8-2004-24.body:
Subtract $CBA$ from $ABC$ column by column. The tens digits are both $B$, so the middle digit never matters: there are 10 choices for it. In the result $495$ the hundreds-minus-hundreds part must give $A - C = 5$ (for example $873 - 378 = 495$ and $601 - 106 = 495$). The pairs are $A = 6, 7, 8, 9$ with $C = A - 5 = 1, 2, 3, 4$ ($A = 5, C = 0$ is not allowed). So there are $4 \times 10 = 40$ possibilities.

**Answer: (B) 40**

cemc-gauss8-2004-25.title: Count by layers
cemc-gauss8-2004-25.body:
Think of the block as $n$ layers, each 11 rows by 10 columns. Inside one layer, each row gives 9 positions and each column gives 10 positions, so $11 \times 9 + 10 \times 10 = 199$ positions per layer, $199n$ in all. A block crossing between two touching layers can sit on any of the $110$ unit squares, and there are $n - 1$ pairs of touching layers: $110(n-1)$ positions. So $199n + 110(n - 1) = 2362$, giving $309n = 2472$ and $n = 8$.

**Answer: (B) 8**

cemc-gauss8-2004-25.title: Count by direction
cemc-gauss8-2004-25.body:
A $2\times1\times1$ block lies along one of the three directions. Along the length-10 direction there are $9 \times 11 \times n$ positions, along the length-11 direction $10 \times 10 \times n$, and along the length-$n$ direction $(n-1) \times 11 \times 10$. Total $99n + 100n + 110n - 110 = 309n - 110 = 2362$, so $n = 8$. Check: $309 \times 8 - 110 = 2472 - 110 = 2362$. ✓

**Answer: (B) 8**
